subject_session: 10 sessions; primary displayed sub-699733573/ses-715093703, GLM on 4 sessions

headline_stat.name: fraction of visual-cortex units orientation-tuned (static gratings, shuffle p<0.01)

verdict: A rigorously controlled, fully reproducible demonstration of cortical orientation selectivity with an in-recording negative control; I would accept it as is.
stated_limitation: Receptive fields were not mapped, so a unit whose receptive field fell outside the monitor counts here as untuned, which makes the cortical fractions a lower bound. ... The GLM was run on four of the ten sessions, the four carrying all three region groups, to keep the compute bounded; the tuning-curve, split-half and decoding analyses use all ten.

justification.dataset: DANDI:000021 (Allen Visual Coding Neuropixels) with drifting/static gratings in mouse visual cortex is the canonical dataset and paradigm for orientation selectivity.
justification.handling: Real data streamed via remfile with the standard Allen unit-QC filters, correct latency-shifted response windows, and a binary-search count that avoids the IntervalSet overlap-merge pitfall on back-to-back static gratings.
justification.analysis: Circular selectivity indices, a drift-preserving block-permutation null, a split-half bias-free population control, a within-recording hippocampal negative control, a confound-adjusted GLM, and cross-validated matched-size decoding are all appropriate and correctly done.
justification.correctness: Every headline value (gOSI medians, tuned fractions, GLM 93%/15%, decoding 53.7%/63.1%, split-half depths 0.57/0.17) reproduces exactly from the committed pickles and is internally consistent and physically possible.
justification.figures: Figures are clearly labeled with units and sample sizes, show the effect and its negative control, and are dominated by full-population summaries rather than flattering single examples.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate to the evidence, a genuine negative control is reported, and a specific limitations section names stimulus-spacing bounds, area-assignment error, unmapped RFs as a lower-bound caveat, and the restricted-session GLM.
